chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Scat and her first jazz record
summary: She never went into scat; the Bob Wilber album was her first jazz record, in her own view, the earlier albums were balladeer work.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I've never gone into the scat business, you know, I mean I can play around with a melody but I don't like the scat lyrics so to speak. I just like to play around with the melody and the harmony and the progressions.
But you do do a little scats on the album with Bob Wilber.

Yeah, there are little bits on "As Long As I Live".
Yeah, that was just thrown in for good measure. I couldn't think of anything else to say.
Okay, when you started out you avoided doing that, I mean, being a jazz singer.
When would you say, did you make your first jazz record?
Oh, maybe after I started singing, the album I made with Bob Wilber, the "Closest Pages In A Book".
Not the '55, '56 material with the Andy Razaf album?
I didn't consider that jazz. It was just, you know, balladeer.
Not the songs with Ellis Larkin and Teddy Wilson in the mid-40's?
You're still doing the same thing that you started out doing?
